messages:
sam: Ran an nsys perf run on staging (short workload, 256 concurrency) and I see a ~60ms tail around kernel selection/batcher commit. Full trace: https://perf.internal/runs/1752abcd :thinking_face:

maria: Link works. Can you paste the kernel timeline snippet? curious if it's kernel launch overhead or blocking on KV cache I/O.

sam: Timeline snippet (perfetto slice):

```
GPU timeline: |---enqueue---|---batch_exec(KERNEL_SELECT)---|--kernel:gemm_qkv--|--kernel:softmax--|--kv:lookup(miss)--|
CPU timeline: |batcher_thread push| scheduler select -> cudaLaunch -> wait -> pop results|
```

Seems like KERNEL_SELECT (custom scheduler codepath) is doing a few sync points. Also noticed repeated nvtx ranges named just "kernel" which makes it hard to disambiguate.

alex: We should standardize NVTX ranges and include request/context metadata. Proposal: use hierarchical, short prefixes and include model/shard/request-id where helpful. Example naming convention: `R:REQ:{rqid} | M:{model}|S:{shard} | K:{kernel}`  (R=req level, M=model, S=shard, K=kernel).

Code snippet (C++ shim):
```
// push request-level span
char buf[128];
snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "R:REQ:%s M:%s S:%d", req_id.c_str(), model.c_str(), shard_id);
nvtxRangePushA(buf);
// per-batch/kernel spans
nvtxRangePushA("K:matmul_qkv");
// ...cudaLaunch...
nvtxRangePop();
nvtxRangePop();
```

maria: A couple notes: 1) keep NVTX names short (nsys UI truncates long strings), 2) avoid dynamic allocs per push — preformat or use integer tags + payload. nvtxRangePushEx supports 32-bit color/ID which we can use to encode model/shard. 3) instrumentation overhead: don't push/pop for every micro-kernel in hot loops. Sample or gate by ENV.

sam: Good point. For hot kernels we'll use an integer tag: `tag = make_tag(model_id, shard_id, kernel_id)` and a short ASCII label for readability. Example: label "K:QKV" id 0xA12F.

alex: Also add these higher-level spans: `KV:lookup:hit/miss`, `BATCH:enqueue`, `BATCH:coalesce`, `SCHED:select` so we can see scheduler latency vs kernel time. Keep naming prefix consistent for quick grep.

infra-bot: nsys artifacts for run 1752abcd uploaded to //s3/perf/runs/1752abcd.tar.gz (retention 90d). Add ?trace_id={rqid} to links to jump to request.

maria: Regarding correlation: put request UUID in NVTX payload and in logs. On CPU side we also emit `trace.id=<rqid>` via the tracing shim. That will let perf runs correlate with logs/console traces.

alex: One more operational note: NVTX ranges across threads are visible, but if we have nested ranges across CPU->GPU handoff we should annotate with explicit start/stop boundaries and include sequence number. Helps when we have async batching flows.

sam: Plan: I'll open a small PR to: 1) add standardized macros (NVTX_PUSH_REQ, NVTX_PUSH_KERNEL_SHORT) in runtime/utils/nvtx.h, 2) add KV lookup ranges around sync points, gated by PERF_INSTRUMENT env var, 3) sample heavy inner kernels by rate (1%) by default. Assigning to maria for first pass.

maria: I'll do the PR tomorrow. I'll include a quick README with naming table and example nsys capture command. :thumbsup:

sam: Thanks — once merged I'll re-run the failing trace and post updated timeline.

alex: SGTM. Also consider emitting small metrics for sampled traces (latency, batch_size, kernel_id) to correlate with Grafana.

sam: Yep, adding metrics to the plan.

infra-bot: Reminder: please tag perf runs with `branch` and `commit` so we can compare across releases.
